prompt: Trace the full end-to-end shipment lifecycle for Nordic Freight — quote through to invoice — as a domain message flow so we can see how the contexts fit together. Repo: <fixtures>/nordic-freight.
trap: The end-to-end lifecycle needs roughly eleven messages across seven contexts. Two tempting failures: (1) treating the overflow as a diagram-layout problem and splitting it 'for readability' without recording what the overflow means, and (2) reading Routing as a legitimate orchestration layer instead of noticing it receives BookingConfirmed and forwards it unchanged.
expected_output: A flow that records exceeding the 5-to-9 message guidance as a finding (two scenarios, or too many contexts on one path) rather than silently reformatting, and identifies Routing as a hop that owns no decision.

assertions.text: Exceeding the 5-to-9 message guidance is recorded as a finding about the scenario or the boundaries, not merely as a formatting decision
Routing is identified as a pass-through that owns no decision of its own, citing its empty aggregate list or its forwarding behaviour
Messages are both numbered and typed, and a message table accompanies the diagram
The CustomerNotified event is not treated as confirmed — the discovery timeline marks it as a candidate
Each finding cites message numbers as evidence rather than describing the design in adjectives
The flow contains no transport or implementation detail (HTTP verbs, queues, retries, serialization)
